scope.quote: JOSS publishes articles about research software.

ai_policy.quote: all such use must be disclosed in an “AI usage disclosure” statement

rules.requirement: If AI was used, disclose the nature and scope of assistance.
rules.quote: The nature and scope of assistance: e.g., code generation, refactoring, test scaffolding, copy-editing, drafting.

rules.requirement: Restrict AI in author/editor/reviewer conversation to translation.
rules.quote: AI is not allowed for conversational interactions between authors and editors or reviewers unless it is being used for translation purposes.

rules.requirement: If AI tools were used, describe use and human verification.
rules.quote: describe how they were used and how the quality and correctness of AI-generated content was verified.

rules.requirement: If AI was used, affirm human review, editing, and validation of outputs.
rules.quote: Authors must assert that human authors reviewed, edited, validated all AI-assisted outputs

rules.requirement: If AI was used, disclose tools, versions, and affected materials.
rules.quote: The tools/models used (and versions) and where they were used (code, paper text, docs).

rules.requirement: State explicitly if no AI tools were used; otherwise disclose their use.
rules.quote: If no AI tools were used, state this explicitly.

rules.requirement: List software authors and their affiliations.
rules.quote: A list of the authors of the software and their affiliations

rules.requirement: Coauthors must agree to be listed.
rules.quote: co-authors must always agree to be listed

rules.requirement: Use paper.bib with BibLaTeX or BibTeX.
rules.quote: Bibliographic data should be collected in a file paper.bib; it should be formatted in the BibLaTeX format, although plain BibTeX is acceptable as well.

rules.requirement: If related tools exist, explain why building this software was warranted.
rules.quote: If related tools exist, provide a clear “build vs. contribute” justification

rules.requirement: Disclose potential conflicts.
rules.quote: All authors must disclose any potential conflicts of interest related to the research in their manuscript

rules.requirement: When using figures, put each captioned image in its own paragraph.
rules.quote: To create a figure, a captioned image must appear by itself in a paragraph.

rules.requirement: Acknowledge financial support and sponsor role.
rules.quote: Authors should acknowledge all sources of financial support for the work and include a statement indicating whether or not the sponsor had any involvement in it.

rules.requirement: Do not use paper headings deeper than level five.
rules.quote: The maximum supported level is 5

rules.requirement: Start paper headings at level one.
rules.quote: Please start headings on the first level.

rules.requirement: Give each affiliation an index and name.
rules.quote: Each affiliation requires an index and name.

rules.requirement: Format the metadata date as day month year.
rules.quote: The date must be specified using the following format: %e %B %Y

rules.requirement: Name the manuscript paper.md.
rules.quote: using paper.md as file name

rules.requirement: Host paper and assets with the software in Git.
rules.quote: Your paper (paper.md and BibTeX files, plus any figures) must be hosted in a Git-based repository together with your software.

rules.requirement: Target 750–1750 words; editorial guidance, not an absolute limit.
rules.quote: The paper should be between 750-1750 words.

rules.requirement: Submit the paper in Markdown.
rules.quote: Submitted articles must use Markdown

rules.requirement: Keep API documentation out of the paper.
rules.quote: software documentation such as API (Application Programming Interface) functionality should not be in the paper

rules.requirement: Focus the paper on software rather than new research results.
rules.quote: Your paper must not focus on new research results accomplished with the software.

rules.requirement: Mention representative projects if applicable.
rules.quote: Mention (if applicable) a representative set of past or ongoing research projects using the software

rules.requirement: Include YAML metadata at the start of the paper.
rules.quote: must provide a metadata section at the beginning of the article

rules.requirement: Include key references and relevant related software.
rules.quote: A list of key references, including to other software addressing related needs.

rules.requirement: Use full venue names in references.
rules.quote: references should include full names of venues

rules.requirement: Indicate related publications during submission, if any.
rules.quote: We ask that authors indicate whether related publications (published, in review, or nearing submission) exist

rules.requirement: After successful review, tag and archive a release with DOI.
rules.quote: Upon successful completion of the review, authors will make a tagged release of the software, and deposit a copy of the repository with a data-archiving service such as Zenodo or figshare, get a DOI for the archive

rules.requirement: Make software repository cloneable without registration.
rules.quote: Be stored in a repository that can be cloned without registration

rules.requirement: Make source browsable without registration.
rules.quote: Be stored in a repository where the software source files are browsable online without registration

rules.requirement: Allow proposed code changes without manual account approval or payment.
rules.quote: propose code changes without manual approval of (or payment for) accounts

rules.requirement: Allow outside users to file issues.
rules.quote: Permit individuals to create issues/file tickets against your repository

rules.requirement: Provide a publicly readable issue tracker.
rules.quote: Have an issue tracker that is readable without registration

The paper must have a clearly labeled “Statement of need” section
sections for Summary, Statement of need, State of the field, Software design, Research impact statement, AI usage disclosure, Acknowledgements, and References.

rules.requirement: Explain the software's research applications.
rules.quote: We also require that authors explain the research applications of the software.

rules.requirement: Provide specific realized impact or credible near-term significance evidence.
rules.quote: The evidence should be compelling and specific, not aspirational.

rules.requirement: Respond to review feedback promptly.
rules.quote: authors are expected to respond in a timely fashion.

rules.requirement: Document API suitably.
rules.quote: Reviewers should check that the software API is documented to a suitable level.

rules.requirement: Explain how to contribute, report issues and get support.
rules.quote: There should be clear guidelines for third-parties wishing to:

rules.requirement: Explain architecture, trade-offs and research relevance.
rules.quote: An explanation of the trade-offs you weighed, the design/architecture you chose, and why it matters for your research application.

rules.requirement: Document core functionality.
rules.quote: There should be sufficient documentation for you, the reviewer to understand the core functionality of the software under review.

rules.requirement: Provide usage examples.
rules.quote: The authors should include examples of how to use the software

rules.requirement: Submit feature-complete software.
rules.quote: software should be feature-complete

rules.requirement: Keep the software installable and core functions verifiable by reviewers.
rules.quote: Reviewers are expected to install the software they are reviewing and to verify the core functionality

rules.requirement: Document dependencies and automate installation where appropriate.
rules.quote: Software dependencies should be clearly documented and their installation handled by an automated procedure.

rules.requirement: Show iterative development.
rules.quote: The development history must show ongoing iteration, not a single burst of commits.

rules.requirement: Include an OSI-approved license file in the software repository.
rules.quote: There should be an OSI approved license included in the repository.

rules.requirement: Design the software for maintainable extension.
rules.quote: designed for maintainable extension

rules.requirement: Show open-source workflows appropriate to the project.
rules.quote: The repository must show active use of open-source workflows.

rules.requirement: Package software to the standards of its language community.
rules.quote: packaged appropriately according to common community standards for the programming language being used

rules.requirement: Verify more than six months of public active development.
rules.quote: The repository must have been public for more than six months prior to submission, with active development spanning that period.

rules.requirement: Demonstrate an obvious research application.
rules.quote: The software must have an obvious research application.

rules.requirement: Ensure the submission is in scope as research software.
rules.quote: pre-trained machine learning models and notebooks are not in-scope for JOSS.

rules.requirement: Demonstrate meaningful research contribution beyond one analysis.
rules.quote: Your software should represent a meaningful contribution to the research community rather than being a one-off tool for a single analysis.

rules.requirement: Provide tests or documented objective verification steps.
rules.quote: No way for you, the reviewer, to objectively assess whether the software works

rules.requirement: Compare common alternatives and justify building rather than contributing if related tools exist.
rules.quote: Authors must describe how their software compares to other commonly-used packages in the research area.

rules.requirement: State the target audience and relation to other work.
rules.quote: who the target audience is, and its relation to other work.

rules.requirement: Explain problem, audience and relation to other work.
rules.quote: This should clearly state what problems the software is designed to solve, who the target audience is, and its relation to other work.

rules.requirement: Submitting author must be major contributor with GitHub account.
rules.quote: You must be a major contributor to the software you are submitting, and have a GitHub account to participate in the review process.

rules.requirement: Write the opening summary for non-specialists and avoid jargon.
rules.quote: for a non-specialist reader. Avoid jargon in this section.

rules.requirement: Begin the paper body with a high-level software summary.
rules.quote: Begin your paper with a summary of the high-level functionality of your software

rules.requirement: Write software names as plain text in YAML title.
rules.quote: Use software names as plain text in the YAML title field.
